name: SINGAPORE

flag.title: Flag of Singapore
flag.note: Red & white, crescent moon, five stars

lead: Singapore is a tiny island city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula. You could drive across it in an hour. Yet it is one of the world's wealthiest nations. It grew from a fishing village to a global hub in two generations.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Singapore is one main island plus 63 smaller ones. It has no mountains. Its highest point, Bukit Timah Hill, is just 164 metres tall.
Singapore has almost no natural resources. It imports nearly all its food and water.
animals: Smooth-coated otters splash through city canals. The Sunda pangolin, the world's most trafficked (illegally sold) mammal, still hides in Bukit Timah and Central Catchment reserves.
Oriental pied hornbills vanished from Singapore by the 1960s. Conservationists put up nesting boxes, and the birds came back. Now 60–100 soar over parks and roadsides.
culture: Food is Singapore's great pride. At hawker centres, big open-air food halls, Chinese, Malay, Indian and Peranakan stalls sit side by side. UNESCO lists them.
Singapore has four official languages: English, Malay, Mandarin and Tamil. Singlish sentences end with "lah", "leh" or "lor". The anthem, Majulah Singapura, is sung in Malay.
history: In 1819, British officer Stamford Raffles chose this swampy island as a free-trade port. Within two years, the population leapt from 150 to 5,000.
Singapore joined Malaysia in 1963 but left two years later. On 9 August 1965, Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew announced independence in tears. It soon became one of the world's richest economies.
wows: Changi Airport has won World's Best Airport 14 times at Skytrax, including 2026.
By purchasing power parity, Singapore's GDP per person is the world's highest.
The Night Safari (1994) was the world's first zoo made only for night visits.
Gardens by the Bay's Flower Dome is the world's largest glass greenhouse.
Singapore's MRT trains are so precise that delays count only from five minutes.
Smaller than London, Singapore is the world's second-busiest container port.
Singapore has grown over 24% bigger since independence by filling in the sea with sand.

myths.myth: You get caned for chewing gum
myths.fact: Caning is not the penalty. Selling gum is banned, but chewing it is legal.
Singapore is its own country. About three in four people have Chinese roots. Many others are Malay or Indian.
